02Why this

The size of it, in your units.

About 3 months booked.
4 or 5 jobs at once, up from 2.

Your numbers, from our two calls on October 9.

You’re turning work away, and the floor has room for more. So the goal is getting more jobs out the door.

A welder can’t start until three things are ready: a drawing, cut steel, and material. One person draws every build. Most cutting goes out to other shops. The interviews, and ten of your job dates, will show which one the welders wait on most.

HOW TO READ IT

  1. 01 · THE TABOne thing a job needs before welding: the drawing, the cut steel, the material.
  2. 02 · THE SLOTThe bay. Each piece drops in when its part is ready. The seam only welds when all three are in.
  3. 03 · THE SEAMThe welder can’t start until all three are ready. The job waits on the last one to show up, however early the other two came.

So speeding up a tab only helps if it’s the late one. The interviews and your job dates find which “tab” is late most often.

03The interviews

Step one is about 15 minutes on a screen.

Each person gets their own link, built for their job. It asks about their week: what they do, what they wait on, and what they wish someone else handled. It takes about 15 minutes, on a phone or a computer.

Nothing to learn.

It is software that asks questions and follows up. They just describe a job in their own words.

Each link fits the person.

You get questions about the whole shop. Jesse gets questions about drawings. Dave gets questions about checks and sign-off.

It hears both sides of a wait.

A welder waits on a kit. The kit waits on a drawing or on cut steel. We hear from both people, the one waiting and the one being waited on, so we can see where the wait starts.

What comes back, and when.

The biggest wait you can change goes first. What already works stays. If the floor is the limit, not the kits, the plan says so.

About 3 weeks after the links open, we walk you through it, at your shop or on a screen: one week for the interviews, two for us to read every answer, check the jobs behind your dates with you, and write the plan. You leave with two things.
